speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I see you've had a rear-end collision resulting in right groin pain and an abnormal leg position; can you describe exactly how your leg was positioned when you were first found?

I also need to know if you were able to move that leg voluntarily or if it feels completely locked in place since the accident.

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) tear and/or medial collateral ligament (MCL) sprain of the right knee with associated hip contusion.

I have noted the mechanism of injury and immediate onset of bilateral knee pain with severe right groin pain. Can you tell me if you felt or heard a "pop" at the moment of the accident, or if your knee gave way when you first tried to bear weight?
